### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/duplicate-record-error.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via resolveSecretField (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/duplicate-record-error.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2b3e3eb671cf020c872d32c817de8bc12da0c476` — the merge of head `fd19d3661bcd7a4ccf2ede82eaa1e5a74e59919c` into base `222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2b3e3eb671cf020c872d32c817de8bc12da0c476 && git checkout 2b3e3eb671cf020c872d32c817de8bc12da0c476
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378 fd19d3661bcd7a4ccf2ede82eaa1e5a74e59919c && git checkout -B drift-repro 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378 && git merge --no-ff fd19d3661bcd7a4ccf2ede82eaa1e5a74e59919c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 222ecc27f9050857d4620e7010d8b85f9d35e378` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fd19d3661bcd7a4ccf2ede82eaa1e5a74e59919c`

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #21274 (body; 5943536760, 5943907420, 5946109461, 5946136544), the cross-lane posts 5943919189 (#21118) and 5946141400 (#6024), PR #21335's body, its 10-file list and the net diff against merge base `c7396f1a99` (the git three-dot diff equals the API diff: 10 files, +1490/-83), head sources through `git show`, and the head's check-runs last. Classes and positions only: no statement, value, sentinel or log line is quoted here.

**The boundary helper** (`packages/objectql/src/driver-fault-redaction.ts` :889 `redactPropagatedDriverFault`) is RIGHT.
- One rule, no copy. Both faces split the dump through the same `splitDriverDump` (:738), the same `statementCut` (:979: the last separator, or the last measured head, so a value that contains the separator can only over-redact, never expose), the same `redactDiagnosticValues` (:1009) and the same `redactStack` (:1067: the header is rebuilt from the first frame line, so a multi-line statement cannot survive in the stack). The log face `redactStatementFromMessage` (:711) was refactored onto `splitDriverDump` and is equivalent to its base form by inspection.
- Each per-shape cut is right. better-sqlite3: `message` and `stack`, its only carriers. node-postgres: `message` and `stack`; `detail`, where a key-shaped line keeps its identifier half so `uniqueViolationColumn` still names the column and any other line is replaced whole; `where` and `internalQuery` replaced whole; the three pg-generic names gated on `severity`. mysql2: `sql` to kind-plus-marker, `sqlMessage` through the measured value templates. The property rules run regardless of the leak predicate, so on a shape whose message is not recognised the properties are still cut; only `message` and `stack` depend on recognition (see ③). The cause chain is cut to depth 4 (:859), the depth the shared predicates read. Nothing statement-bearing is left on any measured shape: `hint`, the pg identifier fields, `code`, `errno` and `sqlState` are value-free as kept.
- The copy keeps the prototype and every own key (symbol-keyed and non-enumerable included, enumerability preserved), is a native Error, never mutates the input, returns the same reference when nothing is cut, and is idempotent on its own output. All pinned in `driver-fault-boundary-redaction.test.ts` across 15 shapes.
- driver-sql's own envelopes (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` :1061, :1126, :1165, :1307) attach `code`, `status`, a non-enumerable `cause` and symbol-keyed flags only; there is no own `sql`, `bindings` or `query` property there for the helper to miss.

**The sites** are RIGHT; no engine exit is missed. Verified on head `engine.ts` by placing every driver call inside an executor closure: find :11878 in [:11862 to :11941]; findOne :12154 in [:12135 to :12209]; insert :13508, :13511 and :13525 (the autonumber-resync creates live in `createWithAutonumberResync` :6404, called only from :13525) in [:12745 to :13694]; update :14355 and :14478 (the prior reads), :15000 and :15297 in [:14022 to :15464]; delete :16660, :16800, :16853 and :16883 in [:16516 to :16986]; count :17030 in [:17027 to :17036]; aggregate :17507 and :17551 in [:17452 to :17553]; `insertMany` :13727 delegates to `insert`. The seam's catch is :5166 to :5177. Outside the seam every driver call is wrapped or classified as the PR's table says: `resolveSecretField` :9052, `resolveInternalField` :9148, `execute` :17616 to :17618 (the await sits inside the try), `ObjectQL.transaction` :17737, `ScopedContext.transaction` :18632. BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK at :17714 and :18767 to :18804 bind no caller value, and driver-sql declares no deferrable constraint, so a commit cannot surface a row. Connect and disconnect (:9589, :10469) and the DDL and introspection paths are outside the ruling's class. The "already safe" rows hold: `SummaryRecomputeError` failures and `insertMany` row outcomes exit through the seam, both pinned. The one other driver call in the package, `lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts` :899 `count`, binds nothing. The `getDriverForObject` out-of-scope row is right as an engine-boundary judgment; its one consequence is flagged in ③.

**The engine's WARN lines** are CONFIRMED unchanged: :13690, :15460 and :16979 still pass `redactBoundStatement(raw)` to `writeFailureLogMeta` inside the executor, before the seam's catch; the control suite pins the meta equal to the raw-derived line on 3 doors by 5 shapes and spells the logged message out for three dialects.

**REST answers** are CONFIRMED: `mapDataError` status, code and `field` are pinned equal raw-versus-cut on all 15 shapes and on the three envelope cases; every shared classifier (`looksLikeInternalErrorLeak`, `isUniqueViolationError`, `uniqueViolationColumn`, `isMissingTableError`) is pinned equal too; `rest-duplicate-record-arm.test.ts` keeps its 409, DUPLICATE_RECORD and field answer unchanged.

**`DuplicateRecordError.cause`** is RIGHT: `field` is computed in the engine from the raw error before the seam, the envelope's own fields are carried, and the cut `cause` keeps its class and code, pinned over sqlite, pg and mysql. `duplicate-record-error.ts` :51 to :57 is a doc edit only.

**The re-judged pins** are RIGHT; nothing is weakened beyond the overturned identity contract. The two `driver-fault-redaction.test.ts` pins now assert both sentinels absent from message and stack, the diagnostic and code kept, and the 400 INVALID_FIELD answer, which is stronger than before. The insert and update suites replace raw identity with prototype, cut-message and code equality through `expectDriverErrorAsItLeaves`; the two nested-envelope pins keep the one-envelope-deep protection (instanceof, `field`, cause not an envelope); the update statement regex flips from must-match to must-not-match with an exact cut form. Counted on the diff: 8 assertion sites in insert, 9 in update, 2 pins in the redaction suite, consistent with the seat's correction of the PR body.

**The auth-library carrier pin** (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/driver-fault-auth-log-carriers.test.ts`) PROVES the ruling's pin: a synthetic sentinel bound through sign-up and update-user against a database-enforced unique index; every console carrier rendered the way `console` renders it plus hidden-field inspect at depth 8; the error objects' properties inspected the same way; the control keeps class, code, `cause.code` and the diagnostic, and the engine WARN carries the marker; the HTTP bodies are checked. SQLite always runs; pg and mysql are `describe.skipIf` on `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` and `OS_TEST_MYSQL_URL` with a named skip, each in its own schema or database. `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/objectql` are already devDependencies of plugin-auth, with five sibling tests as precedent. No `plugin-auth` source edit, as declared on #21118.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/21274-driver-fault-boundary-redaction.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`. RIGHT. `redactPropagatedDriverFault` is exported from its module only; neither published entry (`src/index.ts`, `src/core.ts`; `package.json` exports `.` and `./core`) re-exports it, so no public export is added and the minor precedent does not apply. The prose is accurate against the diff (the site list, the cut and kept sets, the identity note on `cause`, the import-row note) and holds no value: it names the marker and property names only. One wording note, not a defect: "every REST answer keeps its status, code and field" is a claim over the measured set (26 raised errors, 15 pinned shapes) stated as universal.

### ③ Boundary flags

**The dev's open question (A, B, C): A is right, and the fork is declared, not silent.** The ruling's first bullet asks for no statement and no bound values. A keeps one token from a closed four-entry vocabulary (`STATEMENT_KIND` :755, captured by alternation so no other text can ride along): the operation kind, which the door the caller invoked and the error code already disclose; it carries no table, no column and no value, and the shared predicate recognises a dump by exactly that token. In substance the bullet is met. In letter the propagated message is not identical to the log line (it leads with the kind where the log line appends the marker), so "the same redaction" holds for the cut and not for the presentation. B's measured cost (6 of 26 answers relabelled, the SQLite `field` lost) contradicts the ruling's third bullet, and C grows a list the predicate's header rules frozen. The seat's answer A stands; the maintainer may overturn it at the stated cost.

**Deviations**: accepted as recorded in 5946136544. `duplicate-record-error.ts` is a doc comment only; the `rest` test change is one precondition re-judged in the ruling's direction with REST source untouched, declared on #6024; the live databases under `/tmp` are reported stopped by recorded PID and removed, which a diff cannot verify, and the stop-first rule the seat restated applies to the next card.

**The out-of-scope note needs a card.** The residue is real and read-only: `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak` (`packages/types/src/error-leak.ts` :226 to :238) recognises a dump by four leading verbs or a dialect limb, so a raw `execute` (:17616) whose command opens with another verb and whose diagnostic matches no limb is cut on neither face. It is bounded: the property cuts run regardless, so the residue is `message` and `stack` only, through the `execute` door only, because the engine composes its own statements with the recognised verbs. It is still a contract gap inside the ruling's class with a named position, and "the next PR that touches the shared leak predicate" is an unscheduled carrier; Prime Directive #10 says file it. One shape for the fix: the `execute` door knows it bound a statement, so its cut need not consult the predicate. Not a FAIL condition here: pre-existing on both faces, and the measured path is closed.

**One further read-only finding, outside the ruling's class, for a card.** `packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts` `archiveObject` (:1236) reaches the cold store directly through `getDriverForObject` with row data bound (`cold.upsert` :1405, `hot.find` :1373); a driver fault there never crosses a door, and the sweep's caller writes the error's message into the report and a warn line (:683 to :686). Same disclosure class, different route. No auth object declares an archive policy at this head, so it is not p1. The PR's out-of-scope row is right for the engine boundary; the consumer bypassing it is the position to file.
